title: Banking APIs: What They Are and How Finance Teams Use Them
summary: What banking APIs are, the types (data, payments, open banking), how finance teams use them, and why they are the foundation for AI agents in finance.
body_markdown:
For decades, getting data out of a bank meant logging into a portal and downloading a file, or waiting for a statement. **Banking APIs** changed that. They let software connect directly to a bank, programmatically pulling balances and transactions and, in many cases, initiating payments, without a human touching a portal. For finance teams, and especially for the AI agents now running finance work, banking APIs are the pipes that make real-time cash visibility and automation possible.


This guide explains what banking APIs are, the types, how finance teams use them, and why they are the foundation for AI in finance.


## **What is a banking API?**


A banking API (application programming interface) is a secure interface that lets external software communicate directly with a bank's systems. Instead of a person logging in to check a balance or download transactions, an application sends a request to the bank's API and receives the data back instantly, in a structured format. The same mechanism can initiate payments, verify accounts, and more. Banking APIs turn the bank from a website you visit into a system other software can plug into.


> A banking API is the difference between finance software that waits for someone to upload a bank statement and finance software that just knows the balance, continuously, because it is wired straight into the bank.


## **The types of banking APIs**


- **Data APIs.** Pull account balances, transaction history, and statements, the foundation of real-time cash visibility.
- **Payment APIs.** Initiate and track payments (ACH, wire, RTP) programmatically, rather than keying them into a portal.
- **Account verification APIs.** Confirm account ownership and details, used in onboarding and payment setup.
- **Open banking APIs.** Standardized, consent-based APIs (driven by regulation in the UK and EU, and by aggregators like Plaid in the US) that let third parties access bank data with the account holder's permission.


## **How banking APIs reach the bank**


In practice, finance software connects to banks in a few ways:


- **Direct bank APIs.** Connecting straight to an individual bank's API. Powerful but fragmented, since every bank's API is different.
- **Aggregators.** Services like Plaid connect to thousands of banks and expose one unified API, so software integrates once and reaches many banks.
- **Treasury and ERP integrations.** Treasury platforms and ERPs bundle bank connectivity (including legacy protocols like SWIFT and host-to-host), layering it under their own interface.


The right path depends on scale: a startup may use an aggregator, while a multinational treasury connects dozens of banks through a TMS. See[cash management software](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/best-cash-management-software) .


## **How finance teams use banking APIs**


- **Real-time cash visibility.** Pulling balances across all banks continuously, instead of logging into each portal, the foundation of[liquidity management](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/liquidity-management) .
- **Automated reconciliation.** Feeding live bank transactions into reconciliation so the ledger ties to the bank without manual exports.
- **Cash forecasting.** Driving forecasts from actual, current bank data rather than stale downloads.
- **Payments.** Initiating and tracking supplier and other payments programmatically.


## **Why banking APIs are the foundation for AI in finance**


AI agents can only run finance work if they can reach the data, and in finance a huge share of that data lives in the bank. Banking APIs are what let an agent pull live balances and transactions, reconcile against them, build a current cash forecast, and, where appropriate, act, all without a human downloading a file. Without API access to bank data, an AI agent is working from stale, manually exported information; with it, the agent works from the real, current picture.

The banking API is one of the pipes that makes agentic finance real. See[how agents understand enterprise data](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/how-agents-understand-enterprise-data) .


## **Security and banking APIs**


Because banking APIs touch money and sensitive data, security is paramount. Reputable banking APIs and aggregators use encryption, tokenized credentials (so raw bank passwords are not stored or shared), consent-based access, and audit logging. For finance teams, the key is that access is read-appropriate, permissioned, and traceable, the same principles that govern[AI agent access to financial systems](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/ai-agent-governance) .


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is a banking API?**


A banking API is a secure interface that lets external software communicate directly with a bank's systems, pulling balances and transactions and, in many cases, initiating payments, programmatically, without a person logging into a portal. It turns the bank into a system other software can plug into.


### **What are banking APIs used for?**


Real-time cash visibility (pulling balances across banks), automated reconciliation (feeding live transactions to the ledger), cash forecasting from current data, and initiating and tracking payments. They are the foundation for finance automation and AI agents in finance.


### **What is the difference between a banking API and open banking?**


A banking API is any interface to a bank's systems. Open banking is a specific, regulated, consent-based framework (strong in the UK and EU) that requires banks to expose standardized APIs so third parties can access data with the account holder's permission. Open banking APIs are one category of banking API.


### **How do banking APIs support AI in finance?**


AI agents need live access to bank data to work. Banking APIs let an agent pull current balances and transactions, reconcile against them, and build real-time forecasts, instead of relying on stale manual downloads. Without API access, an agent works from outdated data; with it, from the real picture.


## **The bottom line**


Banking APIs are the pipes that connect finance software directly to banks, replacing portal logins and file downloads with live, programmatic access to balances, transactions, and payments. They power real-time cash visibility, automated reconciliation, and current forecasting, and they are the foundation that makes AI agents in finance possible, because an agent is only as good as the data it can reach.
